mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Thursday 4:06 PM ET (US markets closed for Thanksgiving); prices are the 2026-11-25 close (BB.TSX is the Nov 26 TSX price). Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Core Scientific Inc
items.about: Core Scientific runs large data centers, leasing high-density power and space to AI cloud customers alongside its legacy bitcoin mining.
items.why: It slipped 1.5% on Nov 25 after a steep intraday drop, as AI 'neocloud' names sold off on worries about debt-funded data-center buildouts. Posts on Thanksgiving pushed its colocation story (Q3 colocation revenue of about $215M, up roughly 60% from Q2) and claimed a Texas data-center freeze had been lifted, which has not been confirmed.

items.name: Deere & Co
items.about: Deere makes farm, construction and forestry equipment and provides financing for it.
items.why: Deere reported fiscal Q4 on Nov 25. Earnings were $3.89 a share against about $4.03 expected, and its FY2027 net income forecast of $4.5–5.25B came in below estimates. Even so, the stock reversed an early drop and closed up 4.4% at $641, after management said the farm-equipment downturn probably bottomed in 2026. The stream is arguing over why a miss led to a rally.

items.name: Almonty Industries Inc
items.about: Almonty mines tungsten, a strategic metal used in defense and industry, at Sangdong in South Korea and Panasqueira in Portugal.
items.why: The stock was flat, ending at $6.78 after trading between $6.31 and $6.93. The talk is about the Sangdong mine's first concentrate shipments, and posts say a water-treatment fix should get the plant running 24 hours a day by the end of November. Holders also point to a Global X filing for a tungsten miners ETF and the company's planned switch to US GAAP as possible future sources of buying.

items.name: Silicon Motion Technology Corp.
items.about: Silicon Motion designs NAND flash and SSD controller chips used in PCs, phones and data-center storage.
items.why: The stock bounced 2% to $137.75 on Nov 25 after a 12% drop on Nov 24, and it traded as low as $121.66 during Wednesday's chip sell-off. Bulls are citing Q3 revenue of about $560M, up roughly 131% from a year ago on strong SSD-controller demand, while the sentiment gauge remains bearish.

items.name: Analog Devices Inc.
items.about: Analog Devices makes analog, mixed-signal and power chips for industrial, automotive, communications and data-center equipment.
items.why: On Nov 24, ADI posted a record fiscal Q4 with revenue of $4.37B, up about 42% from a year ago, but guided Q1 revenue to roughly flat at about $4.4B with lower margins, and the stock fell. On Nov 25 it rose 6.4% to close at its high of $333. Several brokers trimmed targets after the report (TD Cowen to $375, Needham to $400, Truist to $323), and BMO kept an Outperform rating with a $430 target.

items.name: Hecla Mining Co
items.about: Hecla is the largest US silver producer and also mines gold, lead and zinc.
items.why: Hecla fell about 5% early on Nov 25, then reversed with silver and closed up 3.5% at $11.28 on 36.6M shares. Posts say silver bounced off its 200-day average and a month-end low. One commonly shared data point is that Peru's September silver output fell about 10% from August.

items.name: Nasdaq Inc
items.about: Nasdaq Inc. runs the Nasdaq stock exchanges and sells market data, index licensing and financial-crime software.
items.why: The exchange operator gained 0.6% to $107.07. Most of its chatter comes from traders using the NDAQ ticker to talk about the overall market, including a report that Michael Burry closed his Nasdaq-100 put options, rather than from company news.

items.name: Grayscale Ethereum Mini Trust
items.about: This Grayscale trust holds ether, giving brokerage accounts exposure to the price of Ethereum's token.
items.why: The trust rose 0.8% to $16.10 on Nov 25 as ether bounced a little, but posts note it has dropped roughly 30% since early October. Most of the chatter is about whether crypto still works as a hedge now that institutions dominate the market. Option-promotion posts were disregarded.

items.name: Solaredge Technologies Inc
items.about: SolarEdge makes inverters, power optimizers and batteries for rooftop and commercial solar systems.
items.why: SolarEdge jumped 8.2% to $19.70 on Nov 25 after hitting multi-month lows near $17.30. Posts say a new US tariff on solar panels starting Dec 4 could raise panel prices, and some holders talk up a future catalyst in solid-state transformers. These are crowd claims and no company news was found.

items.name: Workday Inc
items.about: Workday sells cloud software for HR, payroll and finance teams.
items.why: Workday reported fiscal Q3 on Nov 24: revenue of $2.705B (up 11%), non-GAAP EPS of $2.82, and AI product ARR above $750M (up more than 130%). The shares fell about 7% after hours on an outlook seen as only in line, then recovered to close up 0.7% at $180.44 on Nov 25. Bears argue that AI agents could shrink the number of seats HR software can sell.

items.name: GlobalFoundries Inc
items.about: GlobalFoundries is a contract chipmaker producing mature-node chips for autos, phones, IoT and communications.
items.why: GFS dipped 0.6% to $36.20 after recovering from an intraday low of $34.05, in line with the wider chip sell-off on Nov 25. Posts focus on whether foundry demand is recovering and how much the company depends on subsidies, and the sentiment gauge leans bearish. No company-specific news was found.

items.name: Genius Sports Limited
items.about: Genius Sports supplies official sports data, streaming and betting-integrity technology to leagues, sportsbooks and media.
items.why: GENI rose 9.5% to $5.67 on 10.7M shares on Nov 25, with no company news, even as the broader market fell. Posts point to short covering and the company's push for its machine-learning 'Performance Studio', and JPMorgan began coverage recently at Overweight with an $8 target. The stock is still far below its 52-week high of $11.57.

items.name: Altria Group Inc.
items.about: Altria makes Marlboro cigarettes and other tobacco and nicotine products in the US.
items.why: On Thanksgiving morning Altria confirmed it is considering a possible all-cash offer for UK tobacco group Imperial Brands, and said it is talking with an unnamed third party about part of Imperial's business. Imperial says it has not been approached. Under UK rules Altria has until Dec 24 to make a firm bid or walk away. The stock rose 2% to $76.28 on Nov 25, before the news, and holders are now debating how a deal would be funded.

items.name: Hycroft Mining Holding Corp
items.about: Hycroft is exploring and developing a gold-silver deposit in Nevada and is not currently producing.
items.why: HYMC climbed 6.6% to $13.72 on Nov 25 as silver bounced, after losing close to half its value over three months. The stream is split: bulls say silver has bottomed, while bears argue a mining restart would use up its cash. The sentiment gauge reads bearish.

items.name: Okta Inc
items.about: Okta sells cloud identity and access-management software that controls logins for workers, customers and, more and more, AI agents.
items.why: Okta reports earnings after the close on Dec 1, and posts say options are pricing a move of about 13% either way. It rose 1.8% to $201.77 on Nov 25 after rebounding from an early low of $184.57. Debate is about whether identity for AI agents becomes real revenue, and recent filings show a roughly $4.9B contract backlog with 107% net retention.

items.name: Lululemon Athletica Inc
items.about: Lululemon designs and sells athletic apparel, mainly yoga and running wear, through its own stores and online.
items.why: LULU rose 1.3% to $107.44 heading into Black Friday. Its Q3 report is expected in early December, though the company has not confirmed a date. Bulls argue money leaving AI stocks could go to beaten-down retailers, after a strong report from Abercrombie & Fitch, while a pending securities suit over its earlier guidance cuts is also being discussed.

items.name: BlackBerry Ltd
items.about: BlackBerry sells QNX embedded software for cars and machines plus secure communications and cybersecurity tools.
items.why: This is the Toronto listing, which traded on Thanksgiving: it was up 1.3% at C$12.23 late on Nov 26. Posts say some brokers cut BlackBerry's margin requirement to 40–50% from 100%. Holders also cite the CEO's TD Cowen conference remarks that a possible QNX deal with Mercedes is 'not off the table', and a Digital Journal piece on the company moving into physical AI.

items.name: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals Inc.
items.about: Rhythm develops treatments for rare genetic obesity disorders, led by its approved drug Imcivree (setmelanotide).
items.why: RYTM was flat at $119.36 on Nov 25 after a rally of about 34% over the past month. Posts say holders expect a regulatory or label announcement in the first half of December, which the company has not confirmed. Chatter stayed high going into the holiday.

items.name: Palo Alto Networks Inc
items.about: Palo Alto Networks sells firewalls, cloud security and AI-driven security-operations software to businesses.
items.why: Dan McGill, a former regional VP, sued in federal court in New York. He alleges managers pushed resellers to send purchase orders before customers had approved them, so deals could be booked early, and that he was fired for raising concerns. The company calls the claims meritless. The stock closed up 0.9% at $356.14 on Nov 25 and then slipped after hours, days after strong earnings and a $4.5B all-stock deal for Applied Compute.

items.name: Exxon Mobil Corp
items.about: Exxon Mobil is the largest US oil and gas producer and refiner.
items.why: Exxon was flat at $158.08 on Nov 25 while crude kept easing and Brent stayed near $90. Posts note that Exxon says its Guyana output will pass 1 million barrels a day within weeks, and point to Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries. The stock has given back part of its run to about $189 in late October.
